traits.flowering_months.note: iNaturalist research-grade records on GBIF in the south and central Puget Sound lowlands (46.7 to 48.0° N, 122.0 to 123.1° W; counted 2026-10-14): 275 records annotated as flowering (Jan 3, Feb 1, Apr 23, May 100, Jun 86, Jul 37, Aug 2, Sep 5, Oct 6, Nov 9, Dec 3); stated as the months holding at least a tenth of them, May to July. FEIS (Gaultheria shallon) gives May to July for western Oregon and southwestern Washington.

traits.fruiting_months.note: USA National Phenology Network observations (Nature's Notebook) at lowland sites west of the Cascades in Washington and Oregon (below 300 m, west of 121.8° W; 2009 to 2026, fetched 2026-10-14): 49 plant-years at 19 sites seen with ripe fruit, by the months they were seen in (Feb 2, Mar 2, May 2, Jul 16, Aug 20, Sep 20, Oct 11, Nov 8, Dec 4); stated as the months with at least a third as many as the busiest, July to November. FEIS (Gaultheria shallon): ripe from August to October, and the fruit may stay on the stem until December.

traits.height_max_m.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951), as Gaultheria Shallon: grows 60 cm to 2 m tall.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951), as Gaultheria Shallon: leaves 3 cm to 10 cm long.

generator.params.path_half.note: A choice of the model's (crown form step B, broadleaf revision 11): the wood from the base at which a shoot's nodes are half as long, fitted so the plant grows to the height of its oldest reference size, with the crown's width left to grow inside the loose region.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: a dense, spreading evergreen shrub of many arching stems with thick, glossy, finely toothed oval leaves and one-sided racemes of pinkish-white bells. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: Rough sizes from general knowledge of the species: 1.3 m tall at 12 years in the open. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye: dark glossy green leaves; reddish-brown stems; white to pink flowers. Fruit (plant roadmap P4), as in mid-July: racemes of young berries crowned by the calyx, green going dark purple from August. Its year (appearance.organs.bloom.season) takes its days of bud, flower, fruit, ripe and fall from the months it flowers and fruits in, by the rules at the flowering plants (development, 2026-10-14); until then they were authored from general knowledge of the species in the south Puget Sound lowlands: pinkish urn-shaped flowers in May and June; berries green, dark purple from August, eaten into November. The forest's packages show day 196 (mid-July) until the phenology of plant roadmap P5 sets the day from the date and the local climate.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

appearance.organs.bloom.season.flower_lo.note: Its flowers drawn one by one (spec rework L1b): pinkish-white urn-shaped flowers 7 to 10 mm long, drawn as closed urns, opening from the base of each raceme up. From general descriptions of the species (OregonFlora, the Flora of North America and nursery and extension pages as quoted in search results; the pages themselves were not read). The size is the flower's width, or a closed corolla's length, over the fruit's length, roughly as in life.

appearance.organs.bloom.season.opening.note: Days from the first flower of a cluster opening to its last: a third of the days from its first flower to its first fruit as they were set by hand before 2026-10-14, a convention (no source gives a raceme's opening time).

traits.flowering_position.note: FEIS's salal review (page read): terminal and subterminal racemes with bracts.
